newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices hold despite crude selloff.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices hold despite crude selloff.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Monday in lackluster trade, with some light buying interest, particularly at the U.S. Gulf, buoying the complex despite weaker crude, sources said.

"There's not a lot of extra oil in the Gulf, and we're seeing some quiet (buying) interest," said one cash trader, noting firmer USG bunkers, colder Northeast weather this week and some Florida interest also helped boost sentiment.
USG one percent was unchanged at $13.75 a barrel, while three percent firmed a quarter to $12.50 on reports of a small 2.8 percent sale near $13, traders said.
Traders said bids for a one percent and 1.8 percent Florida utility tender were due Tuesday.
In New York Harbor, prices were stable, with physical one percent still at about $15. NYH April one percent paper was little changed at $15.20-45 despite the crude weakness.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also held steady at $16.75-17.00 but relatively cheap East Coast city gate gas prices promised to keep utility interest sluggish near-term.

New York city gate swing gas prices firmed by about five cents Monday to the low-$2.20s/mmBtu area, or about $14.05 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed to the mid-$1.90s/mmBtu, or $12.29 a barrel equivalent.
High sulphurs in New York again were flat from Friday.
